invites-party.title: Invites and party
invites-party.status: Read-only review of the152 assigned tests in25 files at9f045ebca, report6566171808. Rebucketed neighboring cases are not silently approved.
invites-party.keepSummary: letter eligibility and queue parity, correct sigil ownership, phase gates, monotone pulse/route coupling and valid party-guest state
protections: Bursts, cooldowns, chains and piercing share invitation eligibility and queue slots.
Placement, pickup and held-button runs preserve the right sigils and hats.
Before casting and after losing, creatures cannot invite or harm her outside their allowed phase.
Waves, route, forecast and drawing tip stay ordered, bounded and free of NaN.
Guests retain valid destinations, reciprocal partners and distinct stop/destruction behavior.

groups.title: Observed motion and occurrence thresholds
groups.reason: Nine tests pin loaded movement/climb ratios, route drift, treetop swoop frequency, sigil occupancy share, partner arrival, observed poses and the retained noisy picker’s excess crossings. These are outcome-dominated measurements; direct boundaries and ownership must remain separately protected.
groups.question: Move these nine observed motion/occurrence thresholds to nightly/manual reports? Yes retains the measurements and dated comparisons without changing gameplay or dropping direct safety protections.
examples: loaded, she's slower moving away from the pull, not toward it or across it much, and drifts a little toward it
a partner stands beside the one who leads
dancers and idlers near a cluster of placed sigils end up off them
exampleLabels: A loaded witch moves below a sampled speed ratio.
Witches swoop more often near a treetop player.
Dancers rarely occupy a sigil in sampled frames.

groups.title: Mixed party, spread and route statistics
groups.reason: Sixteen mixed tests combine finite-sample extrema, density, activity, route diversity and arrival observations with direct rules. Preserve roster membership, angular bounds/replay, path/floor/seat exclusions, removed-piece absence, caps, deterministic guest places, reciprocal pairs, configured height/40m bounds, finite pulse lifecycle, crossing separation and unoccupied destinations.
groups.question: Split these sixteen tests into blocking rules/integrity checks and nonblocking sampled measurements? Yes preserves bounded geometry, valid ownership, exact replay and route rules; only density/frequency/diversity/timing judgments become reports.
examples: strays each letter within inaccuracy degrees, both ways, and the same every time
deals guests out over the soundsystem and the party places, the same each time
keeps Ed's crossing rules on 40 seeds: at most 4 a map, none the pulse would pass over already drawn ahead of it, 350 m apart (Ed, 2026-10-06)
exampleLabels: Sampled letter spread reaches both sides of the aim.
Guest destinations meet a sampled population share.
Generated routes show a variety of crossing counts.

groups.title: Invitation, phase and route contracts
groups.reason: Direct hit counts use constructed eligible targets, not emergent battles. Phase/state/identity sweeps prevent vacuous passes. Long pulse audits check EVERY step for monotone bounded fronts and exact wave coupling; curveWork is a real planning budget. Old modes remain explicit comparisons.
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
examples: knocked out and teleported home: the line and the pulse don't change
plans quickly on every seed: the curves' untangling kept within its budget (the oak's seed 4 once took 25 s)
holding Use at every morning dressing station and the booth never drops her hat
exampleLabels: Pulse position and wave timing stay coupled at every step.
Route planning stays within its work budget.
A held sigil action preserves the intended interaction.

rulings: Ley-line supersession: old4/5Oct header advances on wave or quest ‘whichever comes first’; the8Oct ruling says ‘The pulse should never skip, it always travels along the route at the bpm speed’. leylines:41/88 explicitly opt into advance=first; :54 tests current default; leyPulseAudit:111 tests both. They are compatibility paths. The audit header saying Ed has not ruled is stale prose, not old behavior.

Witch-count supersession: DESIGN481 drops ‘one new area per witch’ on24Oct. leyPulseAudit:198’s two-witches title actually sets areasPerWave=2 in a SINGLE-witch game. Keep the explicit option’s timing check, but do not claim it proves multiplayer policy;1609 retains that design.

Party guest distinction: an older stopped-soundsystem case flies away;11Oct destroyed-soundsystem design retains the witch stargazing in pairs/threes. partyWitches.gaze:19 checks both ruined and merely stopped; the implementation branches on ruined. No obsolete fly-away assertion was established.
29Oct set-piece removal applies to normal generation; partyDressing:43 does not require any set piece to spawn, and :71 requires removed pieces absent. The title alone is not deletion evidence.

Baby invites changed31Oct. hexSigils:61 starts with already-carried babies; invites:114 uses a level1 stand-in and counting Affection. Neither asserts real baby invitation. Old partyspell prompt prose tests rules input and tool-game compatibility, not a restored start-screen UI.
